primitives.name: PasswordHasher
primitives.purpose: Derive a verifier from a user-supplied secret using a memory-hard KDF with per-credential salt, tunable cost, and constant-time comparison.
primitives.api_signature:
from typing import Protocol

class PasswordHasher(Protocol):
    def hash(self, plaintext: str) -> str: ...
    def verify(self, plaintext: str, stored: str) -> bool: ...
    def needs_rehash(self, stored: str) -> bool: ...
invariants: Stored verifier MUST encode algorithm identifier, cost parameters, salt, and digest so rotation is self-describing.
verify() MUST run in constant time with respect to digest bytes and NEVER branch on character-by-character equality.
Salt MUST be drawn from a CSPRNG, be ≥16 bytes, and MUST NEVER be reused across credentials.
hash() MUST use a memory-hard function (Argon2id / scrypt / bcrypt) and SHALL NEVER use raw SHA-2, MD5, or PBKDF2-SHA1.
needs_rehash() MUST return True when stored cost parameters are below the configured floor, and the caller MUST rehash on next successful login.
Plaintext MUST NEVER be logged, serialized, or included in exceptions raised by this primitive.
primitives.extension_contract: Downstream tools register alternative KDF adapters that implement the Protocol; the adapter declares algorithm id, cost vector, and encoding prefix. The registry refuses to bind an algorithm that lacks constant-time verify or writable cost parameters.

sources.locator: A02:2021 Cryptographic Failures — password storage guidance

primitives.why_essential: A shared hasher forces algorithm, cost, and rotation policy to live in one place; duplicating KDF wiring per tool produces divergent cost floors and eventually a credential store with mixed weak hashes.
alternatives_considered: Per-tool bcrypt call with hardcoded cost — drifts apart over time and blocks coordinated migration.
Pluggable cryptography library passed as dependency — leaks algorithm choice into every caller.
Database-side hashing via pgcrypto — couples auth to a specific data backend and loses constant-time verify.

primitives.name: AuthorizationCodeFlow
primitives.purpose: Execute the OAuth 2.0 authorization-code grant with PKCE, enforcing state, nonce, redirect URI pinning, and one-time code exchange against the token endpoint.
primitives.api_signature:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Protocol

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AuthorizationRequest:
    authorization_url: str
    state: str
    nonce: str
    code_verifier: str

class AuthorizationCodeFlow(Protocol):
    def begin(self, scopes: list[str]) -> AuthorizationRequest: ...
    def exchange(self, code: str, state: str, stored: AuthorizationRequest) -> dict: ...
invariants: begin() MUST generate state and nonce from a CSPRNG with ≥128 bits of entropy and MUST NEVER reuse either value.
exchange() MUST reject any callback whose state does not byte-equal the stored state and SHALL abort before touching the token endpoint.
The code_verifier MUST be bound to the authorization request and CANNOT be substituted at exchange time (PKCE S256).
Redirect URI sent on exchange MUST exactly match the URI registered with the authorization server; wildcard suffixes are FORBIDDEN.
Authorization codes MUST be single-use; replay of the same code SHALL produce an invalid_grant error from the client adapter.
Tokens received MUST NEVER be logged in full; only opaque hashes MAY appear in audit traces.
primitives.extension_contract: New identity providers register as provider adapters implementing the Protocol and publishing metadata (authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, jwks_uri). The registry refuses to bind a provider that does not advertise PKCE S256 and code_challenge_methods_supported.

sources.locator: Section 3.1 Authentication using the Authorization Code Flow

primitives.why_essential: Every tool that accepts federated login needs the same state/nonce/PKCE discipline; reimplementing the dance per integration spawns subtle CSRF and code-injection bugs that no test catches.
alternatives_considered: Implicit flow — deprecated by OAuth 2.1; tokens leak through browser history.
Resource-owner password credentials grant — forbidden by OAuth 2.1 for untrusted clients.
Per-provider bespoke flow in each microservice — guarantees divergent state validation.

primitives.name: TokenIntrospector
primitives.purpose: Validate access tokens by signature, issuer, audience, expiry, and not-before claims, with optional RFC 7662 introspection for opaque tokens.
primitives.api_signature:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Protocol

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TokenClaims:
    subject: str
    scopes: frozenset[str]
    audience: frozenset[str]
    issuer: str
    expires_at: int

class TokenIntrospector(Protocol):
    def introspect(self, token: str, required_audience: str) -> TokenClaims: ...
invariants: JWT verification MUST reject the 'none' algorithm and MUST pin the accepted algorithm set per issuer.
introspect() MUST reject tokens whose aud claim does not include required_audience and SHALL raise a typed error.
Expired tokens (now ≥ exp) and not-yet-valid tokens (now < nbf) MUST be rejected with no claim surface returned.
Signing keys MUST be fetched from the issuer's JWKS with bounded caching; stale keys beyond max-age CANNOT be trusted.
Opaque tokens MUST be introspected against the authorization server per RFC 7662 and NEVER parsed locally.
Introspection results MUST NEVER be cached past the token's exp or past the documented TTL, whichever is lower.
primitives.extension_contract: Token formats register as introspector adapters (JWT, opaque, DPoP-bound) implementing the Protocol. An adapter plugin declares supported issuers and the key resolution strategy; the registry rejects adapters that accept the 'none' alg or skip aud checking.
primitives.why_essential: Each resource server must apply the same claim checks in the same order; scattering verification across controllers yields endpoints that accept tokens meant for another audience.
alternatives_considered: Trust the upstream gateway to verify — leaves services vulnerable if the gateway is bypassed.
Parse JWT inline with a library call per handler — produces inconsistent alg and aud policy.
Always introspect remotely — unacceptable latency for JWT deployments at scale.

primitives.name: WebAuthnAuthenticator
primitives.purpose: Register and assert passkey credentials per the Web Authentication API, binding credentials to an RP ID and verifying attestation, challenge, origin, and signature counter.
primitives.api_signature:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Protocol

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RegistrationResult:
    credential_id: bytes
    public_key: bytes
    sign_count: int
    aaguid: bytes

class WebAuthnAuthenticator(Protocol):
    def begin_registration(self, user_id: bytes, user_name: str) -> dict: ...
    def finish_registration(self, challenge: bytes, response: dict) -> RegistrationResult: ...
    def begin_assertion(self, credential_ids: list[bytes]) -> dict: ...
    def finish_assertion(self, challenge: bytes, response: dict, stored_public_key: bytes, stored_sign_count: int) -> int: ...
invariants: Challenges MUST be ≥16 bytes from a CSPRNG and MUST be single-use; replaying a challenge SHALL reject the response.
The origin in clientDataJSON MUST exactly match the configured RP origin; subdomain or scheme mismatch CANNOT be accepted.
The RP ID hash in authenticatorData MUST equal SHA-256(rp_id); mismatch MUST fail verification.
finish_assertion() MUST reject when the new sign_count is ≤ the stored sign_count, except when the authenticator always returns 0.
User verification flag MUST be enforced for authenticators registered as user-verifying; absence SHALL fail the assertion.
Credential public keys MUST be stored bound to (user_id, credential_id) and NEVER shared across users.
primitives.extension_contract: Attestation formats register as attestation-statement verifiers (packed, fido-u2f, tpm, android-key, apple) implementing a verifier Protocol. The registry refuses to bind a statement type unless it returns an AAGUID and a trust path rooted in a configured metadata service.

sources.locator: Section 7.1 Registering a New Credential; Section 7.2 Verifying an Authentication Assertion
V2.7 Out of Band Verifier Requirements; V2.9 Cryptographic Software and Devices

primitives.why_essential: Passkey onboarding fails in narrow, catastrophic ways (wrong origin, no sign-count check, challenge reuse); a shared primitive encodes the ceremony once so no service can ship a broken variant.
alternatives_considered: Vendor SDK per platform — fragments RP ID policy and challenge storage.
Delegate to hosted passkey provider — loses control of credential export and silent migration.
Stay on TOTP — retains phishable shared secret model the FIDO stack replaces.

primitives.name: TotpVerifier
primitives.purpose: Generate and verify six-digit time-based one-time passwords per RFC 6238 with constant-time comparison, clock-skew tolerance, and replay prevention.
primitives.api_signature:
from typing import Protocol

class TotpVerifier(Protocol):
    def provision_uri(self, account: str, issuer: str, secret: bytes) -> str: ...
    def verify(self, secret: bytes, code: str, last_used_step: int | None) -> int: ...
invariants: Shared secrets MUST be ≥160 bits drawn from a CSPRNG and MUST NEVER be transmitted outside the enrollment channel.
verify() MUST compare codes in constant time and NEVER short-circuit on prefix match.
Accepted skew MUST be bounded to ±1 step (±30s); larger windows SHALL be rejected by configuration.
A successfully used step number MUST be recorded and the same step CANNOT be accepted again for the same secret.
Codes SHALL be six decimal digits derived from HMAC-SHA1 truncation per RFC 4226; alternative digit counts MUST be explicitly opted in.
primitives.extension_contract: Alternative HOTP/TOTP schemes (SHA-256, 8-digit, custom step) register as verifier adapters implementing the Protocol and declaring their digest and period. The registry rejects adapters that skip replay-step persistence.
primitives.consumption_example:
def confirm_mfa(totp: TotpVerifier, user, submitted_code: str) -> None:
    next_step = totp.verify(secret=user.totp_secret, code=submitted_code, last_used_step=user.last_totp_step)
    user.last_totp_step = next_step
    repo.save(user)

sources.locator: Sections 4 and 5 TOTP algorithm and security considerations

primitives.why_essential: Every service that keeps TOTP reimplements the replay-step check and skew window; centralizing the verifier eliminates off-by-one-step bypasses and the classic 'accept any code in the last 10 minutes' bug.
alternatives_considered: SMS OTP only — phishable and deprecated for high-assurance in SP 800-63B.
Email magic link — couples MFA to mailbox security and adds latency.
Per-service TOTP library call — no shared replay protection.

primitives.name: SessionStore
primitives.purpose: Issue, rotate, and revoke server-side session records keyed by high-entropy identifiers, with fixation resistance and explicit lifetime boundaries.
primitives.api_signature:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Protocol

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Session:
    id: str
    subject: str
    created_at: int
    idle_expires_at: int
    absolute_expires_at: int

class SessionStore(Protocol):
    def create(self, subject: str) -> Session: ...
    def load(self, session_id: str) -> Session | None: ...
    def rotate(self, session_id: str) -> Session: ...
    def revoke(self, session_id: str) -> None: ...
    def revoke_all_for_subject(self, subject: str) -> int: ...
invariants: Session ids MUST carry ≥128 bits of entropy from a CSPRNG and MUST NEVER encode user-controlled input.
On privilege elevation (login, role change, MFA step-up) the session id MUST be rotated; the prior id CANNOT be reused.
Sessions MUST expire at min(idle_timeout, absolute_timeout); server-side revocation MUST win over client-held cookies.
Session cookies MUST be set Secure, HttpOnly, and with SameSite=Lax or Strict; Domain SHALL NEVER be broader than the application host.
revoke_all_for_subject() MUST terminate every live session for that subject atomically and MUST be invoked on password change.
load() MUST NEVER extend a session past absolute_expires_at even on activity.
primitives.extension_contract: Storage backends register as session-store adapters (redis, postgres, signed-cookie) implementing the Protocol. Adapters that cannot perform server-side revocation (pure signed cookies) are forbidden from binding when revoke_all_for_subject is required by policy.

sources.locator: V3 Session Management Requirements (V3.2 Session Binding, V3.3 Session Logout)

primitives.why_essential: Fixation, idle timeout, and subject-wide revocation are the shared burden of every authenticated product; without a shared store each team reinvents one missing control and the security posture decays to the weakest.
alternatives_considered: Pure JWT sessions with no server state — cannot revoke without a parallel denylist.
Framework default session middleware — often lacks idle-plus-absolute dual clock.
Sticky-session in memory — fails revoke_all_for_subject under horizontal scale.

primitives.name: CsrfGuard
primitives.purpose: Bind state-changing HTTP requests to the authenticated session through per-session tokens validated against a matching header or form field.
primitives.api_signature:
from typing import Protocol

class CsrfGuard(Protocol):
    def issue(self, session_id: str) -> str: ...
    def verify(self, session_id: str, submitted_token: str) -> None: ...
invariants: Tokens MUST be bound to the session id and MUST NEVER be accepted for a different session.
verify() MUST compare tokens in constant time and MUST raise on mismatch with no information about the expected value.
Safe methods (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS) MUST NEVER mutate state; the guard SHALL only be enforced for unsafe methods.
Cross-origin requests lacking both a valid token and a same-site cookie CANNOT be processed.
Tokens MUST be rotated on session rotation and on explicit logout; stale tokens SHALL be rejected.
primitives.extension_contract: Delivery shapes (double-submit cookie, synchronizer token, custom-header-only for SPAs) register as csrf-strategy adapters implementing the Protocol. The registry refuses to bind a strategy that does not validate Origin/Referer for cookie-only flows.

sources.locator: A01:2021 Broken Access Control — CSRF subsection

primitives.why_essential: CSRF defenses are trivial to get wrong in a single controller; centralizing issuance and verification removes the one endpoint that forgot to bind the token to the session.
alternatives_considered: SameSite=Strict cookies only — blocks legitimate cross-site navigation and is bypassed by subdomain takeover.
Origin header check only — insufficient when Origin is missing (old browsers, same-origin XHR).
Per-form hidden token with no session binding — accepts any valid token from any user.

primitives.name: ContentSecurityPolicy
primitives.purpose: Compose, serialize, and enforce a Content Security Policy header that constrains script, style, frame, and connection origins with strict-dynamic and nonce-based script allowance.
invariants: default-src MUST be set; a policy without default-src CANNOT be rendered.
script-src MUST NEVER include 'unsafe-inline' together with a nonce; the two are mutually exclusive per CSP3.
Nonces MUST be ≥128 bits from a CSPRNG and MUST be unique per response; reuse SHALL invalidate the guarantee.
object-src MUST be set to 'none' unless the caller explicitly opts in with a reason string.
base-uri and frame-ancestors MUST be set to a closed list; wildcard values are FORBIDDEN in production profiles.
report-only and enforce modes MUST be separate header names and MUST NEVER both block and merely report the same directive.
primitives.extension_contract: Per-route policy overrides register as policy-builder decorators that compose on top of a base policy. A decorator is refused if it attempts to widen default-src or reintroduce 'unsafe-inline' on script-src.
primitives.why_essential: CSP rules drift quickly when each team edits its own header string; a composable primitive keeps the baseline coherent and makes 'unsafe-inline' regressions reviewable as a single change.
alternatives_considered: Static nginx header — not nonce-aware; breaks strict-dynamic.
Framework meta-tag CSP — ignored for navigation responses and reporting.
Per-endpoint hand-written header — accumulates divergence and dead directives.

primitives.name: CorsPolicy
primitives.purpose: Evaluate cross-origin preflight and simple-request allowance against a closed list of origins, methods, headers, and credential mode without reflecting arbitrary Origin values.
primitives.api_signature:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Protocol

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CorsDecision:
    allow_origin: str | None
    allow_methods: tuple[str, ...]
    allow_headers: tuple[str, ...]
    allow_credentials: bool
    max_age_seconds: int

class CorsPolicy(Protocol):
    def evaluate(self, origin: str, method: str, requested_headers: tuple[str, ...]) -> CorsDecision: ...
invariants: evaluate() MUST NEVER echo back an Origin that is not in the configured allowlist.
When allow_credentials is True, allow_origin CANNOT be '*' and MUST be a single exact origin.
Vary: Origin MUST be emitted on any response that decides per-origin, or the policy SHALL reject evaluation.
Preflight caching (Access-Control-Max-Age) MUST be ≤86400 seconds and MUST NEVER default to unbounded.
Null origin ('null') MUST be rejected in credentialed mode because it collapses distinct sandboxed contexts.
primitives.extension_contract: Origin matchers register as matcher plugins (exact, suffix-tenant, regex-with-review) implementing a predicate Protocol. The registry refuses to bind a regex matcher that accepts '.*' or an empty pattern.
primitives.consumption_example:
def handle_preflight(policy: CorsPolicy, request, response):
    decision = policy.evaluate(origin=request.headers["Origin"], method=request.headers["Access-Control-Request-Method"], requested_headers=tuple(request.headers.get("Access-Control-Request-Headers", "").split(",")))
    if decision.allow_origin is None:
        response.status = 403
        return response
    response.headers.update({"Access-Control-Allow-Origin": decision.allow_origin, "Access-Control-Allow-Credentials": str(decision.allow_credentials).lower()})
    return response

sources.locator: V14.5 HTTP Request Header Validation Requirements (CORS)

primitives.why_essential: Reflecting Origin is the default footgun of every ad-hoc CORS filter; a primitive with a closed allowlist removes the possibility of writing that line anywhere else.
alternatives_considered: Framework default CORS middleware with origin='*' — incompatible with credentials and leaks data.
Nginx-level CORS — cannot inspect auth state or per-tenant origin lists.
Per-route ad-hoc header writing — reinvents the matcher each time.

primitives.name: OutputEncoder
primitives.purpose: Encode untrusted values for a named sink (HTML text, HTML attribute, JavaScript string, URL path, URL query, CSS value) using sink-specific escaping rules.
primitives.api_signature:
from enum import Enum
from typing import Protocol

class Sink(str, Enum):
    HTML_TEXT = "html_text"
    HTML_ATTRIBUTE = "html_attribute"
    JS_STRING = "js_string"
    URL_PATH = "url_path"
    URL_QUERY = "url_query"
    CSS_VALUE = "css_value"

class OutputEncoder(Protocol):
    def encode(self, value: str, sink: Sink) -> str: ...
invariants: encode() MUST produce output that cannot break out of the named sink; a string encoded for HTML_ATTRIBUTE MUST NEVER enable script execution when inserted into that sink.
The caller MUST declare the sink; the encoder SHALL NEVER infer sink from context.
Encoders MUST be applied at the last possible moment before sink insertion; pre-encoded storage is FORBIDDEN to avoid double-encoding.
CSS_VALUE encoding MUST reject values containing expression()-style sequences and MUST hex-escape control characters.
URL_QUERY encoding MUST percent-encode per RFC 3986 unreserved set; space MUST become %20 inside a path and MAY become + only in form-encoded bodies.
primitives.extension_contract: New sinks register as encoder plugins implementing the Protocol with an extended Sink enum value. A plugin that cannot produce a deterministic context-safe output for its sink CANNOT be bound.

sources.locator: V5.3 Output Encoding and Injection Prevention

primitives.why_essential: XSS is overwhelmingly produced by encoding-in-the-wrong-context; a named-sink encoder makes the sink explicit in every call site and eliminates the 'escape once at ingest' anti-pattern.
alternatives_considered: Template autoescape only — misses JS_STRING and URL_QUERY contexts mixed inside HTML.
Single generic escape function — encodes for HTML_TEXT regardless of sink; unsafe in attributes.
Sanitize on input — loses fidelity and re-introduces bugs when output context changes.

primitives.name: SecretsVault
primitives.purpose: Fetch, cache, rotate, and audit application secrets through a named-secret interface backed by an external key management or secrets service.
primitives.api_signature:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Protocol

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SecretVersion:
    name: str
    version: int
    material: bytes
    not_after: int | None

class SecretsVault(Protocol):
    def get(self, name: str) -> SecretVersion: ...
    def rotate(self, name: str) -> SecretVersion: ...
    def invalidate(self, name: str) -> None: ...
invariants: Secret material MUST NEVER be logged, included in tracebacks, or serialized to telemetry.
get() MUST honor a time-bounded cache; cached material MUST NEVER outlive not_after or the configured max-age.
rotate() MUST produce a strictly increasing version and MUST NEVER return the same material for a different version.
Every get()/rotate() call SHALL emit a structured audit event naming the secret (not the material) and the caller identity.
When the underlying backend is unavailable, the vault MUST fail closed for cold secrets and CANNOT surface stale material past its cache TTL.
primitives.extension_contract: Backends register as vault adapters (AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, GCP Secret Manager, filesystem-for-dev) implementing the Protocol. An adapter is refused if it cannot produce a monotonically increasing version identifier or does not support rotation callbacks.
primitives.why_essential: Secrets scattered in environment variables and config files rotate on no one's schedule; a shared vault primitive makes rotation, caching, and audit a single policy decision rather than a per-service migration.
alternatives_considered: Env vars injected at deploy — no rotation, no audit, leaks into crash dumps.
Per-service SDK call — inconsistent caching and blast-radius controls.
Encrypted config file checked into repo — key management problem reappears one level down.

primitives.name: CryptoEnvelope
primitives.purpose: Encrypt and decrypt payloads with authenticated encryption, key-id-tagged ciphertext, and deterministic header framing that enables key rotation without re-encryption on read.
primitives.api_signature:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Protocol

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Envelope:
    key_id: str
    nonce: bytes
    ciphertext: bytes
    aad: bytes

class CryptoEnvelope(Protocol):
    def seal(self, plaintext: bytes, aad: bytes) -> Envelope: ...
    def open(self, envelope: Envelope, aad: bytes) -> bytes: ...
invariants: seal() MUST use an AEAD construction (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305) and CANNOT emit an envelope without an authentication tag.
Nonces MUST NEVER repeat for a given key; nonce reuse under AES-GCM SHALL be treated as a critical incident.
open() MUST verify aad byte-for-byte; mismatched aad MUST abort before returning plaintext.
key_id MUST resolve to a live key in the vault; decryption with an unknown key_id CANNOT return partial plaintext.
Keys MUST be rotatable without re-encrypting stored ciphertext; open() MUST resolve the correct key by key_id from the envelope.
Plaintext buffers SHALL be zeroed where the runtime allows after use; plaintext MUST NEVER be logged.
primitives.extension_contract: AEAD algorithms register as cipher adapters implementing the Protocol and declaring the nonce size, tag size, and key handle type. The registry refuses to bind an adapter that exposes non-AEAD modes (CBC without HMAC, ECB) or allows nonce reuse.

sources.locator: V6.2 Algorithms (V6.2.4, V6.2.5); V6.3 Random Values
A02:2021 Cryptographic Failures — algorithm and mode selection

primitives.why_essential: Callers that roll their own AES invariably ship CBC-without-HMAC, key-in-cleartext, or nonce-from-timestamp bugs; a shared AEAD envelope moves those decisions out of application code.
alternatives_considered: Raw AES-CBC with HMAC composition — easy to mis-pair; PAD oracle risk.
pgcrypto pgp_sym_encrypt — opaque to app-layer rotation and audit.
Field-level library per model — scatters key policy across schemas.

primitives.name: SignatureVerifier
primitives.purpose: Produce and verify detached digital signatures with key-id selection, typed message framing, and refusal of weak or unannounced algorithms.
primitives.api_signature:
from typing import Protocol

class SignatureVerifier(Protocol):
    def sign(self, message: bytes, key_id: str) -> bytes: ...
    def verify(self, message: bytes, signature: bytes, key_id: str) -> None: ...
invariants: verify() MUST raise on signature mismatch and MUST NEVER return a boolean indicating partial verification.
Accepted algorithms MUST be declared per key_id; algorithm confusion (substituting HS256 for RS256) CANNOT occur.
sign() MUST use deterministic signing (RFC 6979 for ECDSA) or a CSPRNG nonce; ECDSA nonce reuse SHALL be treated as key compromise.
Public keys used for verify MUST be fetched from a pinned trust anchor and MUST NEVER be learned from the same message being verified.
verify() MUST be constant-time with respect to the signature bytes; timing leaks on tag comparison are FORBIDDEN.
primitives.extension_contract: New signature schemes (Ed25519, RSA-PSS, ECDSA-P256, HMAC-SHA256) register as signer adapters implementing the Protocol and declaring their key handle format. The registry refuses to bind adapters for algorithms deprecated by the profile (RSA-PKCS1-v1_5, ECDSA with SHA-1).
primitives.why_essential: Every JWT, webhook, and signed URL uses signatures; without a shared verifier the service accidentally accepts 'alg: none' or compares MACs with != instead of compare_digest.
alternatives_considered: Raw library call per call-site — algorithm confusion bugs stay endemic.
HMAC-only for all signing — does not meet non-repudiation for outbound signatures.
Gateway-terminated signatures only — leaves internal services vulnerable if bypassed.

primitives.name: InputValidator
primitives.purpose: Parse and constrain inbound payloads against a declared schema with typed coercion, length and range bounds, and rejection of unknown fields.
primitives.api_signature:
from typing import Protocol, TypeVar

T = TypeVar("T")

class InputValidator(Protocol):
    def parse(self, raw: object, schema: type[T]) -> T: ...
invariants: parse() MUST reject payloads with unknown fields unless the schema explicitly opts into extras; silent field drop is FORBIDDEN.
Length, range, and pattern bounds MUST be enforced before any business rule touches the value; unbounded strings CANNOT be accepted.
Type coercion MUST be narrowing (string→int only when digits-only); widening coercion (int→string for structured ids) SHALL require explicit opt-in.
parse() MUST raise a typed validation error containing the offending field path; error payloads MUST NEVER include attacker-controlled content verbatim in structured logs.
Recursion depth and collection size MUST be bounded; payloads exceeding the configured limits SHALL be rejected before parsing.
primitives.extension_contract: Schema libraries register as validator adapters (pydantic, attrs+cattrs, msgspec) implementing the Protocol. The registry refuses to bind an adapter that defaults to extra='allow' or that lacks size/depth limits.
primitives.why_essential: Handlers that parse dicts directly forget length limits and leak implementation types; a validator primitive forces schema-first ingress and centralizes the 'reject unknown fields' decision.
alternatives_considered: Manual dict.get() per endpoint — inconsistent bounds and accepts extras silently.
Framework body-parsing with default permissive mode — admits unbounded nested structures.
Regex-only validation — cannot express structural constraints.

primitives.name: RateLimiter
primitives.purpose: Enforce sliding-window request quotas keyed by principal, ip, and route to blunt credential stuffing, enumeration, and brute-force attacks.
invariants: check() MUST be atomic under concurrent callers; lost-update races that under-count requests are FORBIDDEN.
Key composition MUST include a principal identifier and an endpoint selector; rate limits keyed only by IP SHALL be augmented for authenticated requests.
Denied requests MUST return a Retry-After that does not leak internal reset times beyond the window; negative values CANNOT be emitted.
reset() MUST NEVER be callable from unauthenticated request paths; administrative reset is an out-of-band operation.
Authentication endpoints MUST be subject to stricter quotas than general traffic per ASVS V11.
primitives.extension_contract: Storage backends (redis token-bucket, in-memory leaky-bucket, cloud-provider-quota) register as limiter adapters implementing the Protocol. The registry refuses to bind an adapter that does not guarantee atomic check-and-decrement under concurrent access.

sources.locator: V11.1 Business Logic Security Requirements; V2.2 General Authenticator Requirements (anti-automation)

primitives.why_essential: Login endpoints without throttling are a published attack surface; a shared limiter primitive moves the per-endpoint quota decision into configuration and guarantees atomicity no single handler can reimplement wrong.
alternatives_considered: CDN-only rate limits — cannot key on authenticated principal.
Fixed-window counter — allows 2x burst at window boundary.
Per-handler counter in process memory — fails under horizontal scale.

cross_cutting_insights: Authentication primitives (PasswordHasher, WebAuthnAuthenticator, TotpVerifier) all require constant-time comparison; leaving timing discipline to caller code is the single most common implementation failure.
Every credential-facing primitive (hasher, session, vault, envelope) has a rotation dimension; the catalog must treat 'rotatable' as a first-class invariant, not a roadmap item.
OWASP ASVS 4.0.3 V6 (cryptography) and RFC/NIST guidance converge on AEAD, bounded-nonce use, and key-id-tagged ciphertext; the envelope-and-verifier pair is the minimum shared surface.
OAuth 2.0 (RFC 6749), PKCE (RFC 7636), OIDC Core 1.0, and token introspection (RFC 7662) are only safe in combination; pulling any one out reintroduces state-injection or algorithm-confusion bugs.
Session-fixation prevention (ASVS V3) and CSRF binding both require session-rotation plumbing; a split ownership between SessionStore and CsrfGuard reflects that dependency explicitly.

Defense-in-depth at the HTTP edge is three separate policies (CSP, CORS, cookie attributes), not one header; conflating them produces the classic 'unsafe-inline plus credentialed wildcard' failure mode.
Input validation and output encoding are orthogonal: validators constrain shape; encoders constrain sink. Teams that conflate the two end up with either encoded data stored or raw data rendered.
Rate limiting belongs in the security surface, not in resiliency, because NIST SP 800-63B §5.2.2 and ASVS V2/V11 both scope it as an authentication control against automated guessing.
gaps_observed: SKILL-001 lacks a first-class PasswordHasher primitive with rotation-aware needs_rehash semantics; tools that touch credentials inline with bcrypt drift apart.
No WebAuthn/passkey registration primitive — current auth additions assume shared-secret factors and miss origin/RP-ID binding.
CryptoEnvelope with key-id tagging is not surfaced; field-level encryption tools roll their own AES without rotation support.
SecretsVault with rotation and audit hooks is absent; generators rely on environment variables injected at deploy time.
CSP composer is missing; tools emitting HTML responses ship without a nonce-aware, strict-dynamic policy.
RateLimiter is not scoped as a security primitive today; add_rate_limit lives in resiliency and misses principal-keyed login throttling per NIST SP 800-63B §5.2.2.
TokenIntrospector abstraction is absent — JWT verification is reimplemented per tool with inconsistent audience enforcement.
SessionStore lacks a revoke_all_for_subject operation in current tooling; password-change rotation is not guaranteed to terminate live sessions.
